rationale: C22 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template: both are maritime-strike letters to the Attorney General, follow the same Board-of-Inquiry/report/peril/injunction sequence, and share unusually close wording, including “I understand you have a copy of that report” and the expanded “Therefore, in order to remove a peril ... and to secure a resumption ...” transition. C06 is also exceptionally close in operative phrasing, while C10 supplies an earlier maritime-specific version of the same machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: On July 3, 1961, I received the Board's written report in the matter. I understand you have a copy of that report.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: On October 7, 1959, I received the Board's written report in the matter. I understand you have a copy of that report.
shared_material.explanation: Near-verbatim report-receipt language, including the distinctive statement that the Attorney General already has a copy.

shared_material.child_excerpt: In my opinion this unresolved labor dispute has resulted in a strike affecting a substantial part of the maritime industry ... which strike, if permitted to continue, will imperil the national health and safety.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: In my opinion these unresolved labor disputes have resulted in a strike affecting a substantial part of an industry ... which strike, if permitted to continue, will imperil the national health and safety
shared_material.explanation: The same factual and statutory finding is expressed in a closely parallel sentence and applied to a maritime strike.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Therefore, in order to remove a peril to the national health and safety and to secure a resumption of trade, commerce, and transportation ... I direct you ... to petition in the name of the United States any District Court ... to enjoin the continuance of such strike
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Therefore, in order to remove a peril to the national health and safety and to secure a resumption of trade, commerce, transportation or communication ... I direct you ... to petition in the name of the United States any District Court ... to enjoin the continuance of such strike
shared_material.explanation: The operative transition, stated purposes, statutory direction, forum, and requested injunction are nearly verbatim and appear in the same sequence.
